summary: Extends the Message-Context header from RFC 3458 with one more value, "video-message". A receiving mail client can use this as a hint to present the message in the best way.

plainLanguage.summary: The video-message value labels email whose main content is a video, whether the video is attached or referenced externally. A receiving program may use the label as a presentation hint.

subtitle: A Message-Context value for email whose primary content is video.

tldr.problem: Existing Message-Context values did not identify messages whose primary content is video.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC registers video-message as an additional Message-Context value.
tldr.outcome: A receiving user agent may use the value as a hint for presentation; it requires no behavior.

today: RFC 3938 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 3458. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes it.

sections.title: The Message-Context Header
sections.content:
The Message-Context header describes the context of a message and can help a user agent decide how to present it. RFC 3458 registered contexts including voice-message, fax-message, pager-message, multimedia-message, text-message, and none.

This RFC extends that set with a context for video mail.
sections.plainLanguage: A message-context value tells a mail program what kind of message it has. This RFC adds a value for video.

sections.title: Identifying Video Messages
sections.content:
A video message may include the video stream as a body part or refer to a stream stored on a third-party video server. The RFC says neither form is properly identified by the existing message contexts.

The new value is video-message.
sections.plainLanguage: The video may be inside the email or stored elsewhere with a reference. Both forms can use the video-message context.

sections.title: Registration and Security
sections.content:
The RFC registers video-message in the Internet Message Context Types repository for a message whose primary content is video data, or whose main purpose is to reference a video recording.

The header is only a hint. It requires no behavior from a message user agent.
sections.plainLanguage: The new value is added to the context registry. A mail program may use it, but does not have to act on it.

references.text: Burger, E., Candell, E., Eliot, C., and G. Klyne, "Message Context for Internet Mail", RFC 3458, January 2003.
